subject.title: [AI] fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name in…

question: Should OpenClaw accept this source-layer `provider.model` backfill for memory indexes before the broader provider auto-detection work lands?
rationale: The patch is narrow and appears correct, but it changes the canonical model identity used for persisted memory metadata, provider keys, chunk tags, and vector filters when adapters return an empty model.

options.title: Land after upgrade-aware review
options.body: Accept the narrow backfill if maintainers are satisfied that normalizing empty provider models is the intended upgrade behavior for existing memory indexes.

options.title: Request full persisted-index proof
options.body: Ask for a live existing-index reindex plus `memory_search` proof before merge if maintainers want stronger end-to-end storage evidence.

options.title: Pause for broader provider policy
options.body: Hold this PR only if maintainers want the source backfill bundled with the auto-provider migration decision tracked elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Land after upgrade-aware review
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow backfill if maintainers are satisfied that normalizing empty provider models is the intended upgrade behavior for existing memory indexes.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the memory provider adapter boundary introduced in the history for this code path.
